findings.evidence: rg1 (imported with `--fetch`) records 0 of p10's 949 `select.owned_elsewhere` rows (DRIFT copies under `src/agentdojo/defenses/drift/runs/`, owner `drift`); ast-survey-agentdojo likewise 0 of 6 `select.owned_elsewhere` (the AgentHarm `.eval` files, owner ast-survey-agentharm) and 0 of 4 `select.dialect_planned` (`asb/` CSVs). All lie outside the pin's subtree (`runs/`, `agentdojo`): a fetched git-pin tree walks only the pin's subtree, the p10 `--input` import walked the whole local clone. Every file of the snapshot keeps its disposition; executions, verify and the seal forecast are unaffected. p10's origins are `local` (the `--input` route), which `package` refuses (D-33), so the register the spec describes (`D_adapters.md`: the 949 DRIFT copies `select.owned_elsewhere`; the survey's six `.eval` rows) belongs to a route that cannot be sealed. Side effect: these profile excludes (`src/agentdojo/defenses/drift/runs/**`, `agentharm/results/**/*.eval`, `asb/results/*.csv`) can never fire under `--fetch`. R4.
findings.recommendation: Runner/spec owner: state which route defines the register (pin subtree only, or the whole tree), update the D.6.x text and the H.6.2 ownership reading accordingly. No corpus change needed for the seal.
